# Lisbon Apartment Fit for a Remote Worker

## Ranked Options by Overall Fit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

Compact read: the best balance of budget, workability, and commute is **Campo de Ourique** and **Benfica**. The main tradeoff is that the quietest and cheapest options are less central, while the most central options are either noisier or over budget.

| Rank | Option | Rent | Size / Type | Fit Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **E) Campo de Ourique** | **EUR 1490** | 48 m², 1BR, walk-up | Strong all-around fit; quiet residential feel, within budget, likely a manageable transit commute |
| 2 | **C) Benfica** | **EUR 1200** | 60 m², 1BR, near train line | Best value; quieter area, larger space, excellent budget cushion, transit access should be solid |
| 3 | **B) Arroios** | **EUR 1450** | 52 m², 1BR, renovated | Good central convenience and likely easy commute, but area can be busier/noisier than the top two |
| 4 | **A) Alfama** | **EUR 1350** | 38 m², studio, old building | Central and charming, but older building and tourist activity make it weaker for remote-work quietness |
| 5 | **F) Amadora** | **EUR 1100** | 58 m², 1BR, farther out | Cheapest and spacious, but commute likely pushes beyond the 30-minute target |
| 6 | **D) Parque das Nações** | **EUR 1550** | 41 m², studio, modern | Modern and work-friendly, but over the rent cap, so it misses a key priority |

## Why This Order Makes Sense
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

- **1) Campo de Ourique**: Best overall mix of quiet residential character, one-bedroom layout, and rent just under the cap. The walk-up is the main downside, but for a remote worker it is usually less important than daily comfort and neighborhood quality.
- **2) Benfica**: The strongest value pick. It gives you the largest space for the lowest rent among the good-fit options, and the train line should help with center access. This is the best “practical” choice if commute time stays within target.
- **3) Arroios**: Very workable if you want a more central, lively location and a renovated unit. It ranks below Campo de Ourique and Benfica because it is more likely to be noisier and less restful for full-time remote work.
- **4) Alfama**: Great location, but the old building and high-traffic/tourist environment are real drawbacks for quiet work and reliable day-to-day comfort.
- **5) Amadora**: Strong on price and space, but the distance makes the 30-minute transit requirement the biggest risk.
- **6) Parque das Nações**: Normally a strong remote-work area because it is modern, but it misses the rent ceiling, which is a hard constraint in your priorities.

## Tradeoffs to Keep in Mind
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

- **Quietest likely picks:** Campo de Ourique, Benfica
- **Best central convenience:** Arroios, Alfama
- **Best value:** Benfica, Amadora
- **Best building quality / internet confidence:** Parque das Nações, Arroios
- **Biggest risk for remote work:** Alfama’s noise/older building; Amadora’s commute; Parque das Nações’ rent
